title: Yara and the Letters
premise: Sable Hartwell, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter and part-time novelist, has spent ten years rebuilding her life after a public humiliation drove her from her hometown. When she returns for her family's reunion, she hires Yara Okafor, a charming stranger from the mainland, to pose as her partner — but the fake date curdles into something real by dessert, and Yara turns out to be the estranged heir of the development company buying out the harbor, including Sable's lighthouse. As Sable uncovers that Yara has been feeding her family inside information while falling for her, she must decide whether the woman she loves is part of the corruption or its best chance of redemption. In the end, Yara publicly dismantles the buyout at the harbor meeting, and Sable says the sentence she rehearsed for a decade — 'I never stopped belonging here' — before the last ferry of the season carries Yara away, only for Yara to step off it and stay.
about_author: Casper Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing lighthouse logs along the northern coast before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn romances about people who mistake safety for happiness.

chapters.title: The Invitation in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ten years after fleeing her hometown, Sable receives her grandmother's summons to the Hartwell family reunion, the first since the scandal that broke her. She measures her safe, small life in the city and realizes the invitation terrifies her more than her deadline. Beat: fear disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ferry Terminal
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Desperate for a shield, Sable impulsively asks Yara Okafor — a poised stranger waiting at the terminal — to pose as her partner for one weekend, offering cash. Yara hesitates, then agrees with unsettling ease. Beat: a gamble dressed as a joke.

chapters.title: Rules for a Weekend
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the crossing, they negotiate the fiction: how they met, who said what first. Sable invents a love story with suspicious fluency; Yara corrects details as though she's rehearsed them too. Beat: the lie begins feeling collaborative.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Hartwell house is unchanged and unforgiving; aunts catalog Yara like evidence, and Sable's old rival Dana sharpens the reunion's knives. Sable's grandmother watches Yara too carefully. Beat: home as a hostile witness.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At dinner, Dana probes their story and Yara improvises a detail so intimate it lands like truth — the moment Sable's hand finds hers under the table isn't scripted. By dessert they're both performing a relationship they haven't agreed to feel. Beat: the fake becomes real.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable shows Yara the lighthouse she inherited, and the letters her grandfather wrote — the book's namesake — chronicling a love her family disowned. Yara goes quiet in a way that reads as recognition. Beat: intimacy through inheritance.

chapters.title: The Okafor Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara's secret surfaces: she is the estranged heir of Okafor Maritime, the company quietly buying the harbor — including the lighthouse. She came to scout the town under a false name, and the fake date was opportunity, not accident. Beat: guilt with a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Unaware, Sable tells Yara about the humiliation that exiled her — a plagiarized manuscript, a public shaming — and why she stopped trusting her own voice. Yara nearly confesses twice. Beat: vulnerability as countdown.

chapters.title: The Harbor Meeting
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The town learns of the Okafor buyout; the reunion fractures into a war council. Sable's grandmother, who has suspected Yara all along, says nothing — yet. Sable volunteers to lead the resistance, finding her voice again. Beat: purpose rekindled.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara drafts a confession letter to Sable and burns it, then sends a different letter to her father refusing to falsify the lighthouse's structural report. Her family's power, she realizes, runs on people like Sable. Beat: the first betrayal of the family, not the lover.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reveals she has rehearsed one sentence for ten years — 'I never stopped belonging here' — never able to say it aloud. Yara, who knows the truth, urges her to say it now, selfishly, before her own lie detonates. Beat: dramatic irony tightens.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana, digging for ammunition, finds Yara's real identity and the falsified survey timeline, and delivers it to the family — and to Sable — at the worst possible hour. Beat: the knife turns.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at the Light
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts Yara at the lighthouse: every tender moment re-read as reconnaissance. Yara doesn't defend herself; she only asks Sable to read her grandfather's letters and decide if love can survive a corrupted beginning. Beat: heartbreak without cruelty.

chapters.title: What Her Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Grandmother Hartwell's POV. The matriarch reveals she recognized Yara from the start — and let her stay, because she saw in Yara the same exile she once inflicted on Sable's grandfather's beloved. She gives Sable a final letter. Beat: generational mercy.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The grandfather's final letter describes choosing love over a family that demanded loyalty to its own corruption — and warns that belonging must be claimed, not granted. Sable finishes the letter and starts writing her own. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town votes on selling to Okafor Maritime. Yara's father arrives to close the deal personally, using Sable's scandal to discredit the opposition. Yara must choose sides in public, with everything at stake. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Company
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara stands before the town, discloses her identity, the falsified survey, and her father's coercion — burning her inheritance to the ground in real time. Her father's face is the cost; Sable's silence is the worse one. Beat: sacrifice as climax's first strike.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Before the town and her family, Sable says the rehearsed sentence — 'I never stopped belonging here' — claiming the lighthouse, her voice, and her history in one breath, and forgives Yara not for the lie but for the fear behind it. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The buyout collapses; Okafor Maritime withdraws. Yara boards the last ferry of the season, having promised Sable nothing, believing exile is her penance. Sable watches her go and realizes belonging means asking someone to stay. Beat: the ache before the turn.

chapters.title: What Sable Should Have Said
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Alone on the crossing, Yara reads the letter Sable pressed into her hand — a new letter, in the grandfather's tradition, saying everything Sable couldn't say in front of the town. Beat: hope carried across water.

chapters.title: Stepping Off
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At dawn, the ferry makes an unscheduled stop at the harbor's small dock. Yara steps off with one bag and no plan, and Sable — who has spent ten years measuring safe steps — runs the length of the pier. Beat: joy earned.

chapters.title: Yara and the Letters
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. One year later: the lighthouse is a writing retreat, Sable's novel — about a fake date that became real — is finished, and Yara archives the family's letters beside her own. The last line of the book is Sable finally reading her grandfather's first letter aloud. Beat: belonging, chosen daily.
